You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).
  Charts have native data/workbooks, start value axis at zero, and omit an automatic title. Add title and units with text.
table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

header: title, optional subtitle. Measures the installed font and inserts safe line breaks. Title uses
  24-27pt in a two-line band at (0.55,0.22,12.2,0.91); single-line subtitle uses 10-12pt at y=1.18.
  Accent rule y=1.48; put body at y>=1.7. Very long titles/subtitles fail explicitly; keep them concise.
kpi: x,y,w,h,value,label, optional color. Places a large value over its smaller label, with a colored rule.
flow: x,y,w,h,labels (2-5 short strings), optional fill,color. Evenly spaces editable boxes and connectors.
columns: x,y,w,h,items ([{"title":"...","body":"..."}]), optional fill,color. Two to four equal columns,

product: Fictional team scheduling product. Audience is prospective small-team customers. Describe the problem, demonstrate a workflow and close with a specific trial invitation. All performance numbers are synthetic, not customer testimonials.

problem: Pilot survey of 110 teams: 66 report duplicated scheduling work. Treat this as a synthetic survey count, not a market-size estimate.

workflow: Connected sequence: import availability -> flag conflicts -> approve schedule -> notify team. A conflict returns to availability review before approval. Use a visible decision branch.

plans: Starter $21/team/month, 5 members, shared calendar. Pro $52/team/month, 25 members, conflict alerts plus calendar. Enterprise: contact sales, no invented price. Show full comparison as native table.

funnel: Visits 1300, signups 450, trial starts 200, paid teams 80. Trial-to-paid rate 40.0%. Show funnel stages with exact counts; do not imply causal product impact.
6. Benefits
benefits: Availability import reduces manual re-entry; conflict alerts surface overlapping shifts; approval history records who approved a schedule. No quantified time-saving claim is provided.
7. Launch
launch: Beta weeks 1-3; security review weeks 2-4; launch week 6. Launch depends on beta feedback AND security review. Support training remains week 5.
8. Invitation
invitation: Invite a 14-day Pro trial; no payment required. After trial, Pro is $52/team/month. Keep the trial duration and no-payment condition visible.
All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.
Source-specific chart requests take precedence over stylistic chart examples. Rectangles remain axis-aligned.

Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).

table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

header: title, optional subtitle. Measures the installed font and inserts safe line breaks. Title uses

kpi: x,y,w,h,value,label, optional color. Places a large value over its smaller label, with a colored rule.
flow: x,y,w,h,labels (2-5 short strings), optional fill,color. Evenly spaces editable boxes and connectors.
columns: x,y,w,h,items ([{"title":"...","body":"..."}]), optional fill,color. Two to four equal columns,

TASK
Inventory Reorder Protocol for Junior Team Members
Audience: Junior warehouse personnel requiring instruction on restocking protocols
Demonstrate the logical sequence of the restocking protocol to ensure junior staff understand when and how to initiate a reorder.
STYLE: Apply Arial font strictly. Set background to #FFFFFF, text to #000000, and accent to #808080. Focus on dense information density using structured tables and multi-series category charts. Align all elements to a strict baseline grid. Use grayscale rectangles for emphasis without color distraction. The style must appear scholarly, relying on weight and spacing rather than hue for visual hierarchy.
Exactly eight slides, in this sequence:
1. Learning goal
learning_goal: Teach novice stockroom coordinators a simple reorder-point rule. Explain the logic, work through an example, then offer a short practice exercise with its answer.
2. Rule
rule: Reorder point = daily demand x lead time in days + safety stock. Inventory position = on-hand + on-order - committed. Place an order when inventory position is less than or equal to the reorder point.
3. Worked example
worked_example: Daily demand 18 units; lead time 6 days; safety stock 26 units. Reorder point 134 units. Explain each arithmetic step and label units.
4. Inventory
inventory: On-hand 126, on-order 20, committed 17: inventory position 129. It is below reorder point 134, so ORDER. Target position 234; order quantity 105. Preserve on-order and committed values.
5. Process
process: Connected decision: read counts -> calculate inventory position -> compare with reorder point -> ORDER if at/below, otherwise WAIT. The WAIT branch returns to the next daily review.
6. Practice
practice: Exercise: inventory position 146; reorder point 134. Answer WAIT, because the position is 12 units above the trigger. Reveal answer on the slide following the exercise.
7. Misconceptions; first reveal the answer to the previous practice exercise
misconceptions: Do not compare on-hand alone with the trigger. Do not multiply safety stock by lead time. A larger reorder point is a trigger, not the order quantity.
8. Checklist
checklist: Before ordering: verify units, include existing orders, subtract commitments, then check the trigger. Use a simple annotated number line built with editable text and lines.
All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.
Source-specific chart requests take precedence over stylistic chart examples. Rectangles remain axis-aligned.
Use the requested native charts/tables. Judge-visible appearance and content matter; file editability is audited separately.

Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).
  Charts have native data/workbooks, start value axis at zero, and omit an automatic title. Add title and units with text.
table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

Additional optional authoring helpers expand deterministically into the SAME native primitives:
header: title, optional subtitle. Measures the installed font and inserts safe line breaks. Title uses
  24-27pt in a two-line band at (0.55,0.22,12.2,0.91); single-line subtitle uses 10-12pt at y=1.18.
  Accent rule y=1.48; put body at y>=1.7. Very long titles/subtitles fail explicitly; keep them concise.
kpi: x,y,w,h,value,label, optional color. Places a large value over its smaller label, with a colored rule.
flow: x,y,w,h,labels (2-5 short strings), optional fill,color. Evenly spaces editable boxes and connectors.
columns: x,y,w,h,items ([{"title":"...","body":"..."}]), optional fill,color. Two to four equal columns,
  each with a 19pt title and 16pt body. Leave room for text. These helpers do not choose your narrative or content.
Theme colors and fonts are yours to choose. Helpers are optional; all primitive tools remain available.

TASK
Evaluating Strategic Equipment Procurement Paths
Audience: Executive leadership team reviewing long-term asset strategies
Outline distinct procurement pathways for new equipment to facilitate a strategic choice grounded in the provided financial and operational metrics.
STYLE: Select Calibri font for all elements. Background must be #1A1A1A, body text #E0E0E0, and accent #00FF99. Arrange content in grid-like structures using sharp rectangles and straight lines. Display data via native tables or line charts. Ensure high contrast between the dark background and bright neon green accents to evoke a modern, digital system aesthetic without curved connectors.
Exactly eight slides, in this sequence:
1. Decision
decision: Select option B. Investment $366k; annual saving $122k; simple payback 3.0 years; three-year net $0k.
2. Options
options: A/B/C respectively: investment ($k) [214, 366, 528]; annual saving ($k) [79, 122, 173]; uptime (%) 97.8/99.1/99.9. Reference options stay unchanged.
3. Performance
performance: Six monthly outputs M1-M6: [740, 780, 1120, 1030, 1110, 910]; targets [1100, 1100, 1100, 1100, 1100, 1100]; actual total 5690; target total 6600; shortfall 910 units. Show both series in a native chart.
4. Scenario
scenario: Downside/base/upside saving = 80/100/120% of 122: [97.6, 122, 146.4] ($k/year). Payback = investment / saving. Three-year net = 3*saving - investment. Show a scenario chart and the computed paybacks/nets.
5. Capacity
capacity: Sites North/East/West: daily demand [236, 294, 338]; capacity [240, 310, 330]. Preserve all six cells; identify demand above capacity.
6. Roadmap
roadmap: Design weeks 1-2, Build 3-5, Validate 6-8 and Train 6-8 in parallel after Build, gate week 9, rollout weeks 10-13. Both Validate and Train feed the gate. Use connected Technical and People lanes.
7. Gate
gate: GO only if uptime is at least 99.6%, all sites pass capacity validation, and both training and validation finish. Otherwise HOLD. Reference uptime is not proof of operational performance.
8. Risk
risk: Supplier delay: likelihood 4, impact 3, mitigation pre-order critical parts. Training gap: likelihood 2, impact 4, mitigation supervised practice. Show likelihood on x and impact on y, each 1-5.
All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.
Source-specific chart requests take precedence over stylistic chart examples. Rectangles remain axis-aligned.
Use the requested native charts/tables. Judge-visible appearance and content matter; file editability is audited separately.

Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).
  Charts have native data/workbooks, start value axis at zero, and omit an automatic title. Add title and units with text.
table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

TASK
Explanation of Fictional Service Interruption Event
Audience: Internal technical teams analyzing a fictional service outage
Detail the timeline and observed symptoms of the service interruption to assist technical teams in understanding the scope of the event.
STYLE: Choose Calibri font with heavy weights. Background is #0B0C15, primary text #FFFFFF, and accent #FFD700. Create dynamic compositions using oversized bold titles and staggered rectangular accents. Connectors should be thick and straight. Data visualization must use high-contrast solid bars. The layout should feel energetic and impactful, utilizing negative space to highlight key messaging and vibrant yellow accents.
Exactly eight slides, in this sequence:
1. Summary
summary: Fictional service incident. Window 09:00-10:06
2. Impact
impact: 9000 requests in the incident window; 1000 failed (11.1%). Counts refer to requests, not distinct users. Distinct affected users are unknown.
3. Timeline
timeline: 09:00 deployment; 09:08 first alert; 09:17 investigation starts; 09:35 rollback begins; 09:48 rollback complete; 10:06 error rate returns to baseline. Duration 66 minutes. Show events on an editable timeline.

rates: Error rates at 09:00/09:15/09:30/09:45/10:00/10:15: 2/18/25/14/4/1 percent. Preserve all six observations in a line chart; do not equate them with the window-wide rate.
5. Evidence
evidence: Observed: connection pool saturation after deployment and recovery after rollback. Working hypothesis: retry amplification under the new configuration. A causal load test has not yet been completed.
6. Response
response: Detection -> triage -> rollback -> verify baseline -> retrospective. On-call handles rollback; service owner authorizes restoration. Keep verification after rollback, not before it.
7. Actions
actions: Owner A: cap retries by day 10, planned. Owner B: run causal load test by day 7, planned. Owner C: add saturation alert by day 5, complete. Show owner/deadline/status table; do not mark planned actions complete.
8. Lessons
lessons: Separate observed evidence from the root-cause hypothesis. Preserve the distinction between failed requests and affected people. Recovery is verified; preventing recurrence still depends on planned work.
All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.
Source-specific chart requests take precedence over stylistic chart examples. Rectangles remain axis-aligned.
Use the requested native charts/tables. Judge-visible appearance and content matter; file editability is audited separately.

Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).
  Charts have native data/workbooks, start value axis at zero, and omit an automatic title. Add title and units with text.
table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

Additional optional authoring helpers expand deterministically into the SAME native primitives:
header: title, optional subtitle. Measures the installed font and inserts safe line breaks. Title uses
  24-27pt in a two-line band at (0.55,0.22,12.2,0.91); single-line subtitle uses 10-12pt at y=1.18.
  Accent rule y=1.48; put body at y>=1.7. Very long titles/subtitles fail explicitly; keep them concise.
kpi: x,y,w,h,value,label, optional color. Places a large value over its smaller label, with a colored rule.
flow: x,y,w,h,labels (2-5 short strings), optional fill,color. Evenly spaces editable boxes and connectors.
columns: x,y,w,h,items ([{"title":"...","body":"..."}]), optional fill,color. Two to four equal columns,
  each with a 19pt title and 16pt body. Leave room for text. These helpers do not choose your narrative or content.
Theme colors and fonts are yours to choose. Helpers are optional; all primitive tools remain available.

Outline distinct procurement pathways for new equipment to facilitate a strategic choice grounded in the provided financial and operational metrics.
STYLE: Select Calibri font for all elements. Background must be #1A1A1A, body text #E0E0E0, and accent #00FF99. Arrange content in grid-like structures using sharp rectangles and straight lines. Display data via native tables or line charts. Ensure high contrast between the dark background and bright neon green accents to evoke a modern, digital system aesthetic without curved connectors.
Exactly eight slides, in this sequence:
1. Decision
decision: Select option B. Investment $366k; annual saving $122k; simple payback 3.0 years; three-year net $0k.
2. Options
options: A/B/C respectively: investment ($k) [214, 366, 528]; annual saving ($k) [79, 122, 173]; uptime (%) 97.8/99.1/99.9. Reference options stay unchanged.

performance: Six monthly outputs M1-M6: [740, 780, 1120, 1030, 1110, 910]; targets [1100, 1100, 1100, 1100, 1100, 1100]; actual total 5690; target total 6600; shortfall 910 units. Show both series in a native chart.
4. Scenario
scenario: Downside/base/upside saving = 80/100/120% of 122: [97.6, 122, 146.4] ($k/year). Payback = investment / saving. Three-year net = 3*saving - investment. Show a scenario chart and the computed paybacks/nets.
5. Capacity

6. Roadmap

7. Gate

8. Risk

All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.

lessons: Separate observed evidence from the root-cause hypothesis. Preserve the distinction between failed requests and affected people. Recovery is verified; preventing recurrence still depends on planned work.

Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).
  Charts have native data/workbooks, start value axis at zero, and omit an automatic title. Add title and units with text.
table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

TASK
Overview of New Fictional Team Scheduling Platform
Audience: Project managers considering adoption of a fictional planning platform
Illustrate the core capabilities and user interface of the planning platform to enable managers to visualize its integration into current projects.
STYLE: Choose Calibri font with heavy weights. Background is #0B0C15, primary text #FFFFFF, and accent #FFD700. Create dynamic compositions using oversized bold titles and staggered rectangular accents. Connectors should be thick and straight. Data visualization must use high-contrast solid bars. The layout should feel energetic and impactful, utilizing negative space to highlight key messaging and vibrant yellow accents.
Exactly eight slides, in this sequence:
1. Product
product: Fictional team scheduling product. Audience is prospective small-team customers. Describe the problem, demonstrate a workflow and close with a specific trial invitation. All performance numbers are synthetic, not customer testimonials.
2. Problem
problem: Pilot survey of 120 teams: 71 report duplicated scheduling work. Treat this as a synthetic survey count, not a market-size estimate.
3. Workflow
workflow: Connected sequence: import availability -> flag conflicts -> approve schedule -> notify team. A conflict returns to availability review before approval. Use a visible decision branch.
4. Plans
plans: Starter $23/team/month, 5 members, shared calendar. Pro $55/team/month, 25 members, conflict alerts plus calendar. Enterprise: contact sales, no invented price. Show full comparison as native table.
5. Funnel
funnel: Visits 1400, signups 480, trial starts 220, paid teams 88. Trial-to-paid rate 40.0%. Show funnel stages with exact counts; do not imply causal product impact.
6. Benefits
benefits: Availability import reduces manual re-entry; conflict alerts surface overlapping shifts; approval history records who approved a schedule. No quantified time-saving claim is provided.
7. Launch
launch: Beta weeks 1-3; security review weeks 2-4; launch week 6. Launch depends on beta feedback AND security review. Support training remains week 5.
8. Invitation
invitation: Invite a 14-day Pro trial; no payment required. After trial, Pro is $55/team/month. Keep the trial duration and no-payment condition visible.
All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.
Source-specific chart requests take precedence over stylistic chart examples. Rectangles remain axis-aligned.
Use the requested native charts/tables. Judge-visible appearance and content matter; file editability is audited separately.

text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.

  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).

table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

flow: x,y,w,h,labels (2-5 short strings), optional fill,color. Evenly spaces editable boxes and connectors.
columns: x,y,w,h,items ([{"title":"...","body":"..."}]), optional fill,color. Two to four equal columns,

question: Fictional material-screening study: compare treatment with control on pass rate and durability. Random assignment was used, but the study covers one lab and one batch only.

request.prompt:
Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).
  Charts have native data/workbooks, start value axis at zero, and omit an automatic title. Add title and units with text.
table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

TASK
Introducing Fictional Scheduling Tool to Small Teams
Audience: Small team leaders evaluating new fictional scheduling software
Describe the features and intended workflow of the scheduling tool to help leaders assess its potential fit for their team operations.
STYLE: Apply Arial font strictly. Set background to #FFFFFF, text to #000000, and accent to #808080. Focus on dense information density using structured tables and multi-series category charts. Align all elements to a strict baseline grid. Use grayscale rectangles for emphasis without color distraction. The style must appear scholarly, relying on weight and spacing rather than hue for visual hierarchy.
Exactly eight slides, in this sequence:
1. Product
product: Fictional team scheduling product. Audience is prospective small-team customers. Describe the problem, demonstrate a workflow and close with a specific trial invitation. All performance numbers are synthetic, not customer testimonials.
2. Problem
problem: Pilot survey of 110 teams: 66 report duplicated scheduling work. Treat this as a synthetic survey count, not a market-size estimate.
3. Workflow
workflow: Connected sequence: import availability -> flag conflicts -> approve schedule -> notify team. A conflict returns to availability review before approval. Use a visible decision branch.
4. Plans
plans: Starter $21/team/month, 5 members, shared calendar. Pro $52/team/month, 25 members, conflict alerts plus calendar. Enterprise: contact sales, no invented price. Show full comparison as native table.
5. Funnel
funnel: Visits 1300, signups 450, trial starts 200, paid teams 80. Trial-to-paid rate 40.0%. Show funnel stages with exact counts; do not imply causal product impact.
6. Benefits
benefits: Availability import reduces manual re-entry; conflict alerts surface overlapping shifts; approval history records who approved a schedule. No quantified time-saving claim is provided.
7. Launch
launch: Beta weeks 1-3; security review weeks 2-4; launch week 6. Launch depends on beta feedback AND security review. Support training remains week 5.
8. Invitation
invitation: Invite a 14-day Pro trial; no payment required. After trial, Pro is $52/team/month. Keep the trial duration and no-payment condition visible.
All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.
Source-specific chart requests take precedence over stylistic chart examples. Rectangles remain axis-aligned.
Use the requested native charts/tables. Judge-visible appearance and content matter; file editability is audited separately.

Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).
  Charts have native data/workbooks, start value axis at zero, and omit an automatic title. Add title and units with text.
table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

TASK
Findings from Fictional Material Screening Study
Audience: Scientific peers reviewing preliminary experimental screening results
Present the methodology and observed outcomes of a material screening study to enable peer evaluation of the reported patterns.
STYLE: Select Calibri font for all elements. Background must be #1A1A1A, body text #E0E0E0, and accent #00FF99. Arrange content in grid-like structures using sharp rectangles and straight lines. Display data via native tables or line charts. Ensure high contrast between the dark background and bright neon green accents to evoke a modern, digital system aesthetic without curved connectors.
Exactly eight slides, in this sequence:
1. Question
question: Fictional material-screening study: compare treatment with control on pass rate and durability. Random assignment was used, but the study covers one lab and one batch only.
2. Design
design: Two groups, 200 samples each. Equal-duration exposure, same test equipment. Endpoint is passing the predefined strength test. Exclusions were reviewed before final reporting.
3. Results
results: Control passed 116/200 (58.0%). Treatment passed 144/200 (72.0%). Absolute difference 14.0 percentage points. Keep denominators fixed. Show native chart and exact counts.
4. Timecourse
timecourse: Durability at cycles 0/100/200/300: control [100, 87, 73, 59]%; treatment [100, 92, 83, 74]%. Retain all eight values in a line chart.
5. Subgroups
subgroups: Batch labels P/Q/R: treatment pass counts [48, 48, 48]; total 144. Explain that these are counts, not subgroup pass rates because subgroup denominators are not supplied.
6. Audit
audit: Initial extract awaits duplicate-record audit. Do not claim statistical significance or invent a confidence interval.
7. Interpretation
interpretation: The observed treatment pass rate is higher by 14.0 points. This is a measured sample difference, not evidence of broad field performance.
8. Next step
next_step: Replicate in 3 independent labs with blinded scoring. Preserve controls, preregister exclusions, and record batch conditions. A second batch is needed before any deployment claim.
All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.

Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).
  Charts have native data/workbooks, start value axis at zero, and omit an automatic title. Add title and units with text.
table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

Additional optional authoring helpers expand deterministically into the SAME native primitives:
header: title, optional subtitle. Measures the installed font and inserts safe line breaks. Title uses
  24-27pt in a two-line band at (0.55,0.22,12.2,0.91); single-line subtitle uses 10-12pt at y=1.18.
  Accent rule y=1.48; put body at y>=1.7. Very long titles/subtitles fail explicitly; keep them concise.
kpi: x,y,w,h,value,label, optional color. Places a large value over its smaller label, with a colored rule.
flow: x,y,w,h,labels (2-5 short strings), optional fill,color. Evenly spaces editable boxes and connectors.
columns: x,y,w,h,items ([{"title":"...","body":"..."}]), optional fill,color. Two to four equal columns,
  each with a 19pt title and 16pt body. Leave room for text. These helpers do not choose your narrative or content.
Theme colors and fonts are yours to choose. Helpers are optional; all primitive tools remain available.

TASK
Call for Volunteers at Fictional Repair Event
Audience: Community volunteers sought for a fictional repair initiative
Outline the roles and schedule of the repair initiative to motivate potential volunteers to sign up for supporting the event.
STYLE: Use Arial font throughout. Set background to #F5F5F5, text ink to #333333, and accent to #0055A4. Employ generous white space with left-aligned text blocks and thin rectangular dividers. Titles should be large and uppercase. Use simple bar charts with solid fills. Maintain a clean, corporate hierarchy with minimal decorative elements for a professional look.
Exactly eight slides, in this sequence:
1. Purpose
purpose: Fictional neighborhood repair-cafe campaign. Explain who can take part, the event sequence and how to volunteer. Use welcoming language without inventing testimonials or claims about real communities.
2. Capacity
capacity: Four sessions North/East/South/West have seats [50, 43, 34, 49]; total 176. Every session lasts 2 hours. Show all session capacities in a native chart.
3. Volunteers
volunteers: 32 volunteers at 3 hours each = 96 volunteer-hours. Roles: welcome, repair support and safety check. No specialist qualification is implied.
4. Budget
budget: Materials $1340, venue $1000, outreach $680, access support $0; total $3020. Native budget table must preserve each amount and total.
5. Schedule
schedule: Registration opens week 1; training week 2; events week 4; follow-up one week after events, week 5. Event depends on training AND venue confirmation in week 3.
6. Participation
participation: Bring one small household item; repairs depend on available skills and parts. Walk-ins are welcome within session capacity. No guaranteed repair or safety certification.
7. Outcomes
outcomes: Last synthetic trial: 100 items assessed; 60 repaired, 24 referred, 16 not repairable. Counts sum to assessed items. Repair share 60.0%. Keep the synthetic-trial label.
8. Call to action
call_to_action: Sign up as a participant or volunteer by the end of week 2. Events are week 4. Offer a contact placeholder 'Local organizer' without inventing a real address, phone number or website.
All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.
Source-specific chart requests take precedence over stylistic chart examples. Rectangles remain axis-aligned.
Use the requested native charts/tables. Judge-visible appearance and content matter; file editability is audited separately.

question: Fictional material-screening study: compare treatment with control on pass rate and durability. Random assignment was used, but the study covers one lab and one batch only.

design: Two groups, 220 samples each. Equal-duration exposure, same test equipment. Endpoint is passing the predefined strength test. Exclusions were reviewed before final reporting.

results: Control passed 127/220 (57.7%). Treatment passed 157/220 (71.4%). Absolute difference 13.6 percentage points. Keep denominators fixed. Show native chart and exact counts.

audit: Initial extract awaits duplicate-record audit. Do not claim statistical significance or invent a confidence interval.

interpretation: The observed treatment pass rate is higher by 13.6 points. This is a measured sample difference, not evidence of broad field performance.
8. Next step
next_step: Replicate in 3 independent labs with blinded scoring. Preserve controls, preregister exclusions, and record batch conditions. A second batch is needed before any deployment claim.

TASK
Reorder Rule Guide for Novice Stockroom Staff
Audience: New stockroom employees learning basic inventory replenishment rules
Explain the specific steps of the reorder rule clearly so novices can apply the procedure correctly during their shifts.
STYLE: Utilize Georgia font to create a narrative feel. Background should be #FFF8E7, ink #4A3B2A, and accent #C45B3A. Compose slides with centered headings and left-aligned body text blocks. Use soft rectangular shapes behind key points. Charts should use standard bars. The overall composition should resemble a magazine layout with warm, earthy tones and readable serif typography.
Exactly eight slides, in this sequence:
1. Learning goal
learning_goal: Teach novice stockroom coordinators a simple reorder-point rule. Explain the logic, work through an example, then offer a short practice exercise with its answer.
2. Rule
rule: Reorder point = daily demand x lead time in days + safety stock. Inventory position = on-hand + on-order - committed. Place an order when inventory position is less than or equal to the reorder point.
3. Worked example
worked_example: Daily demand 15 units; lead time 5 days; safety stock 22 units. Reorder point 97 units. Explain each arithmetic step and label units.
4. Inventory
inventory: On-hand 89, on-order 20, committed 17: inventory position 92. It is below reorder point 97, so ORDER. Target position 197; order quantity 105. Preserve on-order and committed values.
5. Process
process: Connected decision: read counts -> calculate inventory position -> compare with reorder point -> ORDER if at/below, otherwise WAIT. The WAIT branch returns to the next daily review.
6. Practice
practice: Exercise: inventory position 109; reorder point 97. Answer WAIT, because the position is 12 units above the trigger. Reveal answer on the slide following the exercise.
7. Misconceptions; first reveal the answer to the previous practice exercise
misconceptions: Do not compare on-hand alone with the trigger. Do not multiply safety stock by lead time. A larger reorder point is a trigger, not the order quantity.
8. Checklist
checklist: Before ordering: verify units, include existing orders, subtract commitments, then check the trigger. Use a simple annotated number line built with editable text and lines.
All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.
Source-specific chart requests take precedence over stylistic chart examples. Rectangles remain axis-aligned.
Use the requested native charts/tables. Judge-visible appearance and content matter; file editability is audited separately.

Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).
  Charts have native data/workbooks, start value axis at zero, and omit an automatic title. Add title and units with text.
table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

TASK
Evaluating Strategic Equipment Procurement Paths
Audience: Executive leadership team reviewing long-term asset strategies
Outline distinct procurement pathways for new equipment to facilitate a strategic choice grounded in the provided financial and operational metrics.
STYLE: Select Calibri font for all elements. Background must be #1A1A1A, body text #E0E0E0, and accent #00FF99. Arrange content in grid-like structures using sharp rectangles and straight lines. Display data via native tables or line charts. Ensure high contrast between the dark background and bright neon green accents to evoke a modern, digital system aesthetic without curved connectors.
Exactly eight slides, in this sequence:
1. Decision
decision: Select option B. Investment $366k; annual saving $122k; simple payback 3.0 years; three-year net $0k.
2. Options
options: A/B/C respectively: investment ($k) [214, 366, 528]; annual saving ($k) [79, 122, 173]; uptime (%) 97.8/99.1/99.9. Reference options stay unchanged.
3. Performance
performance: Six monthly outputs M1-M6: [740, 780, 1120, 1030, 1110, 910]; targets [1100, 1100, 1100, 1100, 1100, 1100]; actual total 5690; target total 6600; shortfall 910 units. Show both series in a native chart.
4. Scenario
scenario: Downside/base/upside saving = 80/100/120% of 122: [97.6, 122, 146.4] ($k/year). Payback = investment / saving. Three-year net = 3*saving - investment. Show a scenario chart and the computed paybacks/nets.
5. Capacity
capacity: Sites North/East/West: daily demand [236, 294, 338]; capacity [240, 310, 330]. Preserve all six cells; identify demand above capacity.
6. Roadmap
roadmap: Design weeks 1-2, Build 3-5, Validate 6-8 and Train 6-8 in parallel after Build, gate week 9, rollout weeks 10-13. Both Validate and Train feed the gate. Use connected Technical and People lanes.
7. Gate
gate: GO only if uptime is at least 99.6%, all sites pass capacity validation, and both training and validation finish. Otherwise HOLD. Reference uptime is not proof of operational performance.
8. Risk
risk: Supplier delay: likelihood 4, impact 3, mitigation pre-order critical parts. Training gap: likelihood 2, impact 4, mitigation supervised practice. Show likelihood on x and impact on y, each 1-5.
All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.
Source-specific chart requests take precedence over stylistic chart examples. Rectangles remain axis-aligned.
Use the requested native charts/tables. Judge-visible appearance and content matter; file editability is audited separately.

TASK
Inventory Reorder Protocol for Junior Team Members
Audience: Junior warehouse personnel requiring instruction on restocking protocols
Demonstrate the logical sequence of the restocking protocol to ensure junior staff understand when and how to initiate a reorder.
STYLE: Apply Arial font strictly. Set background to #FFFFFF, text to #000000, and accent to #808080. Focus on dense information density using structured tables and multi-series category charts. Align all elements to a strict baseline grid. Use grayscale rectangles for emphasis without color distraction. The style must appear scholarly, relying on weight and spacing rather than hue for visual hierarchy.
Exactly eight slides, in this sequence:
1. Learning goal
learning_goal: Teach novice stockroom coordinators a simple reorder-point rule. Explain the logic, work through an example, then offer a short practice exercise with its answer.
2. Rule
rule: Reorder point = daily demand x lead time in days + safety stock. Inventory position = on-hand + on-order - committed. Place an order when inventory position is less than or equal to the reorder point.
3. Worked example
worked_example: Daily demand 18 units; lead time 6 days; safety stock 26 units. Reorder point 134 units. Explain each arithmetic step and label units.
4. Inventory
inventory: On-hand 126, on-order 20, committed 17: inventory position 129. It is below reorder point 134, so ORDER. Target position 234; order quantity 105. Preserve on-order and committed values.
5. Process
process: Connected decision: read counts -> calculate inventory position -> compare with reorder point -> ORDER if at/below, otherwise WAIT. The WAIT branch returns to the next daily review.
6. Practice
practice: Exercise: inventory position 146; reorder point 134. Answer WAIT, because the position is 12 units above the trigger. Reveal answer on the slide following the exercise.
7. Misconceptions; first reveal the answer to the previous practice exercise
misconceptions: Do not compare on-hand alone with the trigger. Do not multiply safety stock by lead time. A larger reorder point is a trigger, not the order quantity.
8. Checklist
checklist: Before ordering: verify units, include existing orders, subtract commitments, then check the trigger. Use a simple annotated number line built with editable text and lines.
All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.
Source-specific chart requests take precedence over stylistic chart examples. Rectangles remain axis-aligned.
Use the requested native charts/tables. Judge-visible appearance and content matter; file editability is audited separately.

Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.

table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

kpi: x,y,w,h,value,label, optional color. Places a large value over its smaller label, with a colored rule.
flow: x,y,w,h,labels (2-5 short strings), optional fill,color. Evenly spaces editable boxes and connectors.

product: Fictional team scheduling product. Audience is prospective small-team customers. Describe the problem, demonstrate a workflow and close with a specific trial invitation. All performance numbers are synthetic, not customer testimonials.

problem: Pilot survey of 120 teams: 71 report duplicated scheduling work. Treat this as a synthetic survey count, not a market-size estimate.

workflow: Connected sequence: import availability -> flag conflicts -> approve schedule -> notify team. A conflict returns to availability review before approval. Use a visible decision branch.

plans: Starter $23/team/month, 5 members, shared calendar. Pro $55/team/month, 25 members, conflict alerts plus calendar. Enterprise: contact sales, no invented price. Show full comparison as native table.

funnel: Visits 1400, signups 480, trial starts 220, paid teams 88. Trial-to-paid rate 40.0%. Show funnel stages with exact counts; do not imply causal product impact.

benefits: Availability import reduces manual re-entry; conflict alerts surface overlapping shifts; approval history records who approved a schedule. No quantified time-saving claim is provided.
7. Launch
launch: Beta weeks 1-3; security review weeks 2-4; launch week 6. Launch depends on beta feedback AND security review. Support training remains week 5.
8. Invitation
invitation: Invite a 14-day Pro trial; no payment required. After trial, Pro is $55/team/month. Keep the trial duration and no-payment condition visible.
All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.

Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).
  Charts have native data/workbooks, start value axis at zero, and omit an automatic title. Add title and units with text.
table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

TASK
Introducing Fictional Scheduling Tool to Small Teams
Audience: Small team leaders evaluating new fictional scheduling software
Describe the features and intended workflow of the scheduling tool to help leaders assess its potential fit for their team operations.
STYLE: Apply Arial font strictly. Set background to #FFFFFF, text to #000000, and accent to #808080. Focus on dense information density using structured tables and multi-series category charts. Align all elements to a strict baseline grid. Use grayscale rectangles for emphasis without color distraction. The style must appear scholarly, relying on weight and spacing rather than hue for visual hierarchy.
Exactly eight slides, in this sequence:
1. Product
product: Fictional team scheduling product. Audience is prospective small-team customers. Describe the problem, demonstrate a workflow and close with a specific trial invitation. All performance numbers are synthetic, not customer testimonials.
2. Problem
problem: Pilot survey of 110 teams: 66 report duplicated scheduling work. Treat this as a synthetic survey count, not a market-size estimate.
3. Workflow
workflow: Connected sequence: import availability -> flag conflicts -> approve schedule -> notify team. A conflict returns to availability review before approval. Use a visible decision branch.
4. Plans
plans: Starter $21/team/month, 5 members, shared calendar. Pro $52/team/month, 25 members, conflict alerts plus calendar. Enterprise: contact sales, no invented price. Show full comparison as native table.
5. Funnel
funnel: Visits 1300, signups 450, trial starts 200, paid teams 80. Trial-to-paid rate 40.0%. Show funnel stages with exact counts; do not imply causal product impact.
6. Benefits
benefits: Availability import reduces manual re-entry; conflict alerts surface overlapping shifts; approval history records who approved a schedule. No quantified time-saving claim is provided.
7. Launch
launch: Beta weeks 1-3; security review weeks 2-4; launch week 6. Launch depends on beta feedback AND security review. Support training remains week 5.
8. Invitation
invitation: Invite a 14-day Pro trial; no payment required. After trial, Pro is $52/team/month. Keep the trial duration and no-payment condition visible.
All data are synthetic. Preserve the given facts and caveats. Show conclusions, units and useful arithmetic.
Source-specific chart requests take precedence over stylistic chart examples. Rectangles remain axis-aligned.
Use the requested native charts/tables. Judge-visible appearance and content matter; file editability is audited separately.

request.prompt:
Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).
  Charts have native data/workbooks, start value axis at zero, and omit an automatic title. Add title and units with text.
table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

Additional optional authoring helpers expand deterministically into the SAME native primitives:
header: title, optional subtitle. Measures the installed font and inserts safe line breaks. Title uses

kpi: x,y,w,h,value,label, optional color. Places a large value over its smaller label, with a colored rule.
flow: x,y,w,h,labels (2-5 short strings), optional fill,color. Evenly spaces editable boxes and connectors.
columns: x,y,w,h,items ([{"title":"...","body":"..."}]), optional fill,color. Two to four equal columns,

table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.

Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

flow: x,y,w,h,labels (2-5 short strings), optional fill,color. Evenly spaces editable boxes and connectors.
columns: x,y,w,h,items ([{"title":"...","body":"..."}]), optional fill,color. Two to four equal columns,

Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),

table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

header: title, optional subtitle. Measures the installed font and inserts safe line breaks. Title uses

kpi: x,y,w,h,value,label, optional color. Places a large value over its smaller label, with a colored rule.
flow: x,y,w,h,labels (2-5 short strings), optional fill,color. Evenly spaces editable boxes and connectors.
columns: x,y,w,h,items ([{"title":"...","body":"..."}]), optional fill,color. Two to four equal columns,

Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).
  Charts have native data/workbooks, start value axis at zero, and omit an automatic title. Add title and units with text.
table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

Additional optional authoring helpers expand deterministically into the SAME native primitives:
header: title, optional subtitle. Measures the installed font and inserts safe line breaks. Title uses
  24-27pt in a two-line band at (0.55,0.22,12.2,0.91); single-line subtitle uses 10-12pt at y=1.18.
  Accent rule y=1.48; put body at y>=1.7. Very long titles/subtitles fail explicitly; keep them concise.
kpi: x,y,w,h,value,label, optional color. Places a large value over its smaller label, with a colored rule.
flow: x,y,w,h,labels (2-5 short strings), optional fill,color. Evenly spaces editable boxes and connectors.
columns: x,y,w,h,items ([{"title":"...","body":"..."}]), optional fill,color. Two to four equal columns,
  each with a 19pt title and 16pt body. Leave room for text. These helpers do not choose your narrative or content.
Theme colors and fonts are yours to choose. Helpers are optional; all primitive tools remain available.

Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.

Inventory Reorder Protocol for Junior Team Members
Audience: Junior warehouse personnel requiring instruction on restocking protocols
Demonstrate the logical sequence of the restocking protocol to ensure junior staff understand when and how to initiate a reorder.
STYLE: Apply Arial font strictly. Set background to #FFFFFF, text to #000000, and accent to #808080. Focus on dense information density using structured tables and multi-series category charts. Align all elements to a strict baseline grid. Use grayscale rectangles for emphasis without color distraction. The style must appear scholarly, relying on weight and spacing rather than hue for visual hierarchy.
Exactly eight slides, in this sequence:
1. Learning goal
learning_goal: Teach novice stockroom coordinators a simple reorder-point rule. Explain the logic, work through an example, then offer a short practice exercise with its answer.
2. Rule
rule: Reorder point = daily demand x lead time in days + safety stock. Inventory position = on-hand + on-order - committed. Place an order when inventory position is less than or equal to the reorder point.
3. Worked example
worked_example: Daily demand 18 units; lead time 6 days; safety stock 26 units. Reorder point 134 units. Explain each arithmetic step and label units.
4. Inventory
inventory: On-hand 126, on-order 20, committed 17: inventory position 129. It is below reorder point 134, so ORDER. Target position 234; order quantity 105. Preserve on-order and committed values.
5. Process
process: Connected decision: read counts -> calculate inventory position -> compare with reorder point -> ORDER if at/below, otherwise WAIT. The WAIT branch returns to the next daily review.
6. Practice
practice: Exercise: inventory position 146; reorder point 134. Answer WAIT, because the position is 12 units above the trigger. Reveal answer on the slide following the exercise.
7. Misconceptions; first reveal the answer to the previous practice exercise
misconceptions: Do not compare on-hand alone with the trigger. Do not multiply safety stock by lead time. A larger reorder point is a trigger, not the order quantity.
8. Checklist
checklist: Before ordering: verify units, include existing orders, subtract commitments, then check the trigger. Use a simple annotated number line built with editable text and lines.

Return ONE JSON object, no markdown, executable code or explanation.
You control the entire 8-slide, 16:9 deck. Coordinates are inches on a 13.333333 x 7.5 canvas.
Native editable PowerPoint objects are generated from this scene. Use at most 28 elements/slide.
Schema: {"theme":{"background":"FFFFFF","ink":"172B4D","accent":"007F86","font":"Arial"},
"slides":[{"background":"FFFFFF","elements":[...]}]}. Theme and slide background are optional.
Colors are six hex digits without #. Use only installed fonts Arial, Georgia or Calibri.
Each element has type plus these fields (no other element types):
text: x,y,w,h,text,size (points),color,bold (bool),align (left/center/right). Optional fields use size=18, theme ink.
rect: x,y,w,h,fill; optional line (color),radius (bool). Rectangles contain no text; add a text object.
line: x,y,x2,y2,color,width (points). Lines are native connectors.
chart: x,y,w,h,kind (bar/column/line),categories (strings),series ([{"name":"...","values":[numbers]}]),
  optional colors (one hex per series),size (axis/data text points, default 14),legend (bool),labels (bool).
  Charts have native data/workbooks, start value axis at zero, and omit an automatic title. Add title and units with text.
table: x,y,w,h,rows (rectangular array of strings), optional size (default 14),header_fill,header_color,fill,color.
  First row is the header. All rows have equal height. Cells wrap; leave enough space.
Numbers must be finite. Put every object inside the canvas. Text wraps with a small fixed margin.
No automatic content repair, layout optimization, font shrinking or factual correction occurs.
Keep all facts accurate. Aim for a polished deck: hierarchy, alignment, contrast, restrained color,
legible labels and purposeful charts/diagrams. Vary layouts with the story. Make the decision easy to find.
Stay below 75,000 characters of JSON. Do not add author/model/tool names. No external assets or web access.

Additional optional authoring helpers expand deterministically into the SAME native primitives:
header: title, optional subtitle. Measures the installed font and inserts safe line breaks. Title uses

flow: x,y,w,h,labels (2-5 short strings), optional fill,color. Evenly spaces editable boxes and connectors.
columns: x,y,w,h,items ([{"title":"...","body":"..."}]), optional fill,color. Two to four equal columns,
